question: The department says that the aggregate behaviour of 14 personas across 4 repos follows mathematical laws. How wide is the uncertainty on an aggregate of 14, and what does shared context do to it?
production_path: investigation: read the department record, the personas folder, state/council and its schema at the pinned commit; found 17 persona files against the 14 stated, and no record in which more than two reviewers answer one question

takeover: an interrupted author session had left extract.py, observed-input.json, scenarios.json and analyze.py; each was read, rerun and compared with its previous output before being kept or rewritten, so the hypothesis below was written after that inherited analysis had been run once, except its last clause, which was written before the second model was computed

extract: snapshot the record's claim, the persona names, the council reviews, the schema's limit and the two files of the tribunal panel into observed-input.json, refusing any source file whose Git blob differs from the pin
model: exact Clopper-Pearson intervals by binomial summation and bisection; a copy model in which agents share a signal with pairwise correlation rho; design effect and effective sample size

test: the exact mixture distribution against the variance formula, a seeded simulation of 50,000 occasions per correlation, a second generating model (beta-binomial) in exact fractions, and the length of the decision log that would detect a correlation

adversarial: three negative controls (a planted review by a persona, the Wald interval through the coverage test, a simulation scored against the wrong correlation), rounding-boundary and comparison-margin checks, and the objection that the model and its correlations are invented

investigation, late: a search for the word tribunal, made while rereading the review brief, found a workflow that would send one pull request to a panel of 5 personas; section 1 was corrected and the log sizing repeated for 5 agents, after writing these predictions: with logs of 20 occasions, under 95% detect rho 0.3 (guess 65%) and under 40% detect rho 0.1 (guess 22%); with logs of 100, over 95% detect rho 0.3 and under 95% detect rho 0.1 (guess 55%)

adversarial: the first 5-agent sizing, on 50,000 occasions, gave 95.2% and 40.3%, against the first two predictions; twelve reruns with other seeds and other code, outside the fixture, averaged 35.9% at rho 0.1 with a standard deviation of 2.1 points, so that simulation was enlarged to 200,000 occasions and every detection share is also stored for the two halves of its logs; on the larger run the four directions hold and the three guessed magnitudes were far too low
test: byte-identical reruns on Windows (CPython 3.9, 3.12, 3.14) and Linux (CPython 3.14), 64 self-checks, five answered exercises and an answer-free transfer task

revision after an independent agent review (no human reviewer): the workflow file's own comment on failed runs, which says the lane 'silently never produced a verdict', is now snapshotted and quoted instead of describing the panel only as not run; the normal approximation's 385 agents is checked against the exact binomial share of occasions within 5 points, 94.7% at 385 and at least 95% for every group from 399 to 1,000
hypothesis: For 14 independent yes/no agents the exact 95% interval at an even split is wider than half of the scale, and a shared cause with a pairwise correlation of 0.3 leaves fewer than 3 effective agents under a ceiling of 1/rho that no group size raises; the variance and the effective sample size depend only on the correlation, while the probability of a unanimous answer changes by more than a factor of two with the generating model.
evidence: Observed at Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8: the department record states 14 personas across 4 repos, and the snapshot holds 17 persona files and 4 consumer repos; its only recorded answers of several reviewers to one question are 5 council verdicts on one pull request with at most 2 reviews each (9 reviews, none by a persona). One workflow would send a pull request to a panel of 5 personas, each with a concern of its own and three possible answers, all given the same title, body, file list and diff excerpt; a comment in its workflow file says the lane 'silently never produced a verdict', and its verdict folder does not exist at that commit: no recorded occasion has 14 personas, or 5, answering about a common object.

Computed from assumed inputs: the exact 95% interval for 7 yes among 14 independent agents is 0.230 to 0.770 (width 0.539), against 0.398 to 0.602 for 50 of 100 and 0.490 to 0.510 for 5,000 of 10,000; a half-width of 5 points needs 385 independent agents by the normal approximation (counted exactly, 385 land within it on 94.7% of occasions), and 5 unanimous independent agents bound the yes probability only above 0.478.

Synthetic: in a copy model with pairwise correlation rho, 14 agents have an effective sample size of 6.087 at rho 0.1, 2.857 at 0.3 and 1.591 at 0.6, under a ceiling of 1/rho at any group size; the exact variance equals p(1-p)/n * (1 + (n-1) rho) to 1e-12, and 50,000 simulated occasions per correlation give variance ratios of 0.990, 2.291, 4.926 and 8.792 against design effects of 1, 2.3, 4.9 and 8.8.

Synthetic: the exact interval that assumes independence contains p = 0.5 on 98.7%, 90.6%, 64.5% and 20.4% of occasions at rho 0, 0.1, 0.3 and 0.6; a beta-binomial model with the same correlations has exactly the same variance but makes a unanimous answer 2.2 to 3.9 times as likely (10.7% against 2.8% at rho 0.3), so the tail figures depend on the model.

Synthetic sizing of the measurement that would settle the question, at p = 0.5 for exchangeable yes/no agents: logs of 20 occasions exceed the threshold set by independent logs in 92.5% of 2,500 simulated logs at rho 0.1 for 14 agents and, for 5 agents, the panel's size, in 36.1% of 10,000 at rho 0.1 and 94.5% at rho 0.3 (logs of 100 occasions: 1,759 of 2,000, 88%, at rho 0.1). No decision of any persona was read, this study did not run the tribunal panel and no correlation between personas was estimated, so the answer stays conditional on an unmeasured rho; when this record was written (2026-10-13), no human subject review, learner trial, translation or publication of this course existed, and research duration was not instrumented: duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
